relevance_note: The cohort contains one patient with a TNFAIP3 mutation ('TNFAIP3 (P22)') who is described at individual level in Table 1, Tables S1-S4 and the text ('One patient with a TNFAIP3 mutation who was clinically diagnosed with type I diabetes'), so an in-scope person with a TNFAIP3 variant is reported; the paper gives him no HA20 diagnosis.
method_note: Read the paper Markdown including the converted supplementary tables S1-S4. Every value was transcribed by hand from the Markdown; no script transcribed any table. Scope: this is a 26-patient IEI cohort covering ten genes; only P22, the single patient with a TNFAIP3 mutation, is in scope, so the other 25 patients get no rows and are counted in cohort_size_as_stated. The 26 patients are counted by 25 rows in Tables S3/S4 (no P5, P11, P13, P14, P21 rows); I could not reconcile this with the stated 26 patients. No table cell in this paper contains values stacked as ' / ', so no stacked-cell (D-31) problem arose and nothing was read positionally. No relatives of P22 are described (the Methods only say 'The parents of each patient provided written informed consent'), and no family history, parental testing or consanguinity is given, so inheritance is not reported. Contradictions and oddities found in the paper: (1) Table 1 prints P22's mutation cell as 'TNFAIP3:c.2152del(40m)Hypergly', i.e. the first word of the next column is merged into it, while Table S2 prints the same variant as 'TNFAIP3:c.2152del'; (2) Table 1 gives P22's sex as M, whereas Tables S3 and S4 both give F for P22 - because of this I did not use the Table S3/S4 'Age' value ('4Y') for age_at_last_evaluation and left that field not reported; (3) the same variant is called 'a TNFAIP3 mutation' and 'a heterozygous mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene', and no A20 haploinsufficiency or TNFAIP3-deficiency diagnosis is given to P22, so no HA20 checklist feature is taken from the disease label; (4) for autoantibodies, the text says 'routine evaluation of autoantibodies was also negative' for P22 while the microarray showed 'significant increases in the levels of several autoantibodies' - under D-27 I recorded the routine-assay result as an excluded row naming what it rules out ('autoantibodies detected by routine clinical assay') and kept the checklist item 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' observed from the microarray result, since the two statements are about different assays rather than a present/absent contradiction; (5) 'elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)' was left not reported because the paper reports autoantibody findings only; (6) skin lesions (checklist) were set to observed from 'Eczema'; (7) blank cells in P22's Table 1 row (Infection, Digestive symptom, Lymphoproliferative) were left not reported; (8) Table 1 is the source of the 'not reported'-free individual fields; the diagnosis is called 'Type 1 Diabetes' in Table 1 and 'type I diabetes' in the text, and I kept the Table 1 spelling for disease_label_as_stated.

feature_text_as_stated.span: In patient P22, who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, routine evaluation of autoantibodies was also negative, but the results of a microarray revealed significant increases in the levels of several autoantibodies, including those against alpha-actinin, troponin-I, islet antigen 2 (IA2), interferon-alpha1 (IFN-A1), interferon-beta (IFN-B), LPS, La/SSB, and angiotensin II receptor (AGTR).
